title: AgFunder Research: Agrifoodtech Investment Reports and Intelligence
answer: AgFunder Research is a publisher page from AgFunder, an investor in food and agriculture, describing its agrifoodtech research and intelligence output. It says AgFunder publishes periodic investment reports, emerging market studies, climate trend work, country deep dives and startup guides, alongside AgFunderNews. The most useful single point is that global agrifoodtech funding reached $16.2 billion in 2025, almost flat at -3% versus the prior year, with investors becoming more selective and directing capital toward companies with tangible science, real unit economics and clear revenue paths.

sections.body: AgFunder publishes this research page. The text says that as part of AgFunder's role in funding startups in food and agriculture, it has become a leading agrifoodtech research and intelligence source. It provides daily news coverage through AgFunderNews and publishes periodic research on trends shaping the future of food and agriculture. Its research includes investment reports on venture capital funding to foodtech and agtech startups, emerging market agrifoodtech and climate trends, country deep dives and resource guides for startups. The supplied text does not state a publication date. It is a commercial research landing page from an investor in the sector.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: AgFunder describes itself as a leading agrifoodtech research and intelligence source, publishing periodic research alongside daily news through AgFunderNews. Its research includes investment reports on venture capital funding to foodtech and agtech startups, emerging market agrifoodtech and climate trends, country deep dives and resource guides for startups. On funding, the page says global agrifoodtech funding hit $16.2 billion in 2025, almost flat versus the prior year at -3%, but with a notable shift in where the money went. Investors are writing checks more selectively, directing capital towards companies with tangible science, real unit economics and clear paths to revenue. Developing markets agrifoodtech funding grew substantially between 2023 and 2024 at 63%, versus a 4% decline in global agrifoodtech. Global agrifoodtech showed some signs of recovery in 2024, reaching $16 billion, just a 4% drop from 2023. Increased investment in developed markets such as the US and the Netherlands, and developing nations like India, hint at better days to come, though no one is out of the woods yet. APAC agrifoodtech startups raised $4.2 billion as of the end of October 2024, a 38% increase on the $3.1 billion raised over the same period in 2023. African agrifoodtech funding raised $145 million in the first half of 2024, a 1.6% year over year increase, but still just 1.6% of global investment. This followed a 2023 decline of 62% to $275 million. Deals remained almost flat, with 129 closing in 2023 compared to 133 in 2022, indicating smaller deal sizes.

sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: The source does not mention artificial intelligence. For a reader following AI in agriculture, its value is as a broad agrifoodtech funding barometer. It shows overall investment levels, regional shifts and investor priorities such as tangible science, real unit economics and clear paths to revenue. Those priorities can frame how agrifoodtech companies are assessed, but the source does not separate AI from other categories. It should be used for context on the funding climate, not as evidence of AI specific investment totals or trends.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Agriculture

sections.body: The source is a research landing page, not a full report. It gives summary figures without methodology, source citations or a stated publication date. It covers agrifoodtech broadly and does not break out artificial intelligence or other technology segments. It is published by AgFunder, which funds startups in food and agriculture, so it has a commercial interest in the sector. The regional figures are partial snapshots, such as APAC to the end of October 2024 and Africa for the first half of 2024. It does not provide enough detail to verify the numbers or to track individual deals.
